answer: In the agent economy, every identity must continuously publish a cryptographic mirror of its private challenge-response log, committing to unique behavioral history. An attacker spinning up N sybil identities must generate and maintain N independent mirror chains in parallel; under concurrent load this forces the attacker’s available cores to their compute nadir, while any mismatched commitment is instantly sable-flagged and slashable, so the marginal cost scales linearly with the number of fakes and an honest single agent pays only ordinary continuous verification.
